source_text.body:
Migrate a codebase from Solid to React with parallel agents
Cursor ran hundreds of agents on one codebase for weeks, doing an in-place Solid-to-React migration (+266K/-193K edits) that passed CI but still needed careful review.
Done with
CR
Cursor
What they did
Cursor pointed its multi-agent system at its own codebase for an in-place Solid-to-React migration. Planner agents explored the code and created tasks, and sub-planners covered specific areas. Worker agents each took one task and pushed changes to the same branch, while a judge agent decided at the end of each cycle whether to continue. Earlier designs with locks and flat self-coordination had failed.
How it went
The migration took over three weeks and made +266K/-193K edits. It passed CI and early checks, but the authors say it still needs careful review.
Worth knowing
The post says prompts mattered more than the harness or models. It also says agents sometimes ran far too long and needed periodic fresh starts to counter drift.
Try it yourself
with
Cursor
Copy prompt
I want to migrate my codebase at [repo path] from [source framework, e.g. Solid] to [target framework, e.g. React] in place. First write a migration plan that splits the work into independent chunks by [directory or feature], then run background agents on those chunks in parallel. Each chunk is done when it builds and the existing tests pass. Finish with a summary of what changed and which files most need my careful review, and don't merge anything until I've looked at it.
Original source: https://cursor.com/blog/scaling-agents
